text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak discusses with Libyan Leader Muammar Gaddafi the stalled peace process and confirms the importance of an Arab common market.
- The Saudi-owned Asharq al-Awsat daily apologises to Mubarak's businessmen sons, Alaa and Gamal, and confirms its confidence in their innocence.

Mubarak's sons have complained to the public prosecutor's office about an advertisement in the daily that included allegations of corruption and monopolistic practices. The advertisement was part of a publicity campaign for the daily's new magazine al-Jadida.

- Mubarak says a resolution by the U.S. House of Representatives to move the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem from Tel Aviv is not wise. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says the joint Egyptian-Libyan committee has discussed the creation of a free-trade zone to boost trade exchange between the two countries.

- The ministry of irrigation has decided to provide water for 1.085 million acres (440,000 hectares) to grow rice in the summer season, Shukri Gamal, manager of the ministry's water distribution, said.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says no strategic projects will be privatised. "There will be no privatisation at all of strategic projects, which are important for the national security, particularly military industries," he adds.
